links.outcome: Fairness (TPR, FPR, F1 disparities) across sex, age, and race for stigma detection models
links.effect: Supervised fine-tuning models showed greater bias than ICL models in zero-shot, 4-, 8-, and 16-shot settings on TPR, FPR, and F1 disparities; disparities were present in some models.
links.quote: Under the conditions tested, fairness evaluation revealed that supervised fine-tuning models exhibited greater bias compared with ICL models in the zero-shot, 4-shot, 8-shot, and 16-shot settings, as measured by true positive rate, false positive rate, and F<sub>1</sub>-score disparities.

unlisted_practices: Using in-context learning LLMs to detect stigmatizing language in clinical notes
Data-efficient few-shot approaches when labeled data are scarce

screen.reason: The study evaluates the technical performance and fairness of different in-context learning prompting strategies and baseline models for automated detection of stigmatizing language in EHR text on an offline benchmark dataset.
